note: SMART configurations captured from public servers, each entry present because it exercises something the shared adapter has to get right. 'source' is where it came from, so the live test can re-fetch it; 'usable' is whether discovery should accept it. Adding a server means adding an entry here and nothing else.

servers.label: PCIS GOLD
servers.note: Sends response_types_supported and management_endpoint as null. Nothing reads either, and everything needed to authorize is present and absolute, so refusing the document would have refused a server this backend can use.

servers.label: CHN Tech Solutions
servers.note: Sends scopes_supported as a list containing a list. Seen on three unrelated vendors' deployments of the same underlying server, so one upstream slip reaches many endpoints.

servers.label: Carepaths
servers.note: Publishes relative endpoints ('/login'). Refused rather than resolved against the host we were handed, which is how a check becomes an open redirect.

servers.label: Medical Informatics Engineering
servers.note: Serves a FHIR CapabilityStatement at the SMART configuration path, so there is no authorize endpoint to find. Its resource list is truncated here; nothing reads it.

configuration.name: MIE_Base_FHIR_Capability_Statement
configuration.title: IIMC Capability Statement
configuration.description: This is the Capability Statement for FHIR in system IIMC.

software.name: Webchart EHR by Medical Informatics Engineering

servers.label: Radysans
servers.note: Publishes the endpoints as explicit nulls. Reachable, and still nothing to send a user to. The server has since published real endpoints, so this is a historical capture: it still covers the null-endpoint shape, but re-fetching it would no longer reproduce it.

servers.label: ONC Inferno reference server
servers.note: Advertises private_key_jwt alone, so a confidential client is refused rather than sent a secret the server will not accept. A public client authorizes normally.

servers.label: interop.community sandbox
servers.note: Advertises no PKCE, so no code_challenge is sent. Also names the auth methods key without its _supported suffix, which is ignored rather than misread.

servers.label: CMS Blue Button 2.0 sandbox
servers.note: Advertises no token endpoint auth methods at all, which falls back to Basic. A payer rather than an EHR.

servers.label: Medplum
servers.note: Publishes no revocation endpoint, so disconnecting is local-only. Its issuer is also the API root rather than the FHIR base.

servers.label: athenahealth preview
servers.note: Names an issuer on an entirely different host from the FHIR base, confirming aud tracks the issuer we were given rather than the one discovered.

servers.label: athenahealth
servers.note: The largest single vendor in the national list by endpoint count.

servers.label: Practice Fusion
servers.note: Publishes the sparsest usable document in the corpus: the two endpoints and almost nothing else.

servers.label: Oracle Health
servers.note: A production tenant, where the authorize and token endpoints sit on a different host from the FHIR base.

servers.label: Altera Digital Health
servers.note: Self-hosted per organization rather than multi-tenant, so the endpoint is the practice's own domain. Sends management_endpoint as an empty string, which is the third distinct way this corpus publishes an optional field wrong.

servers.label: TruBridge
servers.note: Stands in for the vendors serving thousands of endpoints that refuse an unauthenticated request for their configuration.

servers.label: Modernizing Medicine
servers.note: Gives every tenant its own subdomain, so the issuer host itself varies per organization.
